system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:38, WS-DWELLS-01 recorded a network logon for kim.ortega from WS-KORTEGA-01, and the later PowerShell process used the same logon ID.

At 13:40:23, kim.ortega ran the specific Install-MonthlyPatches.ps1 script from the FILE-LV-01 IT share. This matches the organization’s stated patching practice and scheduled monthly workstation patching, so the PowerShell activity has a plausible authorized explanation.
The PowerShell process launched wusa.exe to install a Windows update package; a proxy record shows a large Windows Update download shortly beforehand, and both processes later exited.

During the same period, 10.20.20.30 resolved WS-DWELLS-01’s name and initiated a connection to the workstation’s RPC endpoint mapper on port 135; the connection ended with RST. The inventory identifies 10.20.20.30 as the web proxy, while remote administration is stated to come from WS-KORTEGA-01.

Near the end of the review window, process-exit records show Google Drive File Stream and GlobalProtect processes under dana.wells’s account. These are not among the listed approved services, but the records do not establish what they were used for or whether they are related to the PowerShell event.

known_telemetry_limitations: The evidence records the PowerShell command line but does not include the patch script’s contents, hash, signature, or file-share audit history.
The available process records do not establish whether the PowerShell window was visible to dana.wells.
The proxy-to-workstation RPC connection is recorded, but the evidence does not identify its initiating process or explain why it originated from the proxy.
The supplied records are a subset of activity; absence of other suspicious events in this set does not establish that none occurred.
claims_not_established: Whether the patch script and the update package were authentic and unmodified.
Whether the proxy-originated RPC connection was authorized, accidental, misattributed, or malicious.
Whether the Google Drive File Stream or GlobalProtect processes transferred data or provided remote access.
Whether any of these activities caused dana.wells to see the reported PowerShell window.
additional_evidence_needed: Confirm with IT whether kim.ortega performed the scheduled patching on WS-DWELLS-01 and obtain the CHG-2291 or patch-deployment execution records.
Collect the exact Install-MonthlyPatches.ps1 version, hash, signature, and FILE-LV-01 share-access or file-audit records for the execution.
Investigate the 10.20.20.30-to-WS-DWELLS-01 port 135 connection using proxy and network-device logs, including source-process or connection attribution.
Review endpoint execution and network history for Google Drive File Stream and GlobalProtect to determine whether they were used and whether data or remote-access sessions occurred.
